S86.08.needs: a paired phone (Mobile app) and a signed-in account; a second paired device is not shown in this panel
S86.08.note: The VS Code panel lists only the one connected phone and offers Disconnect, not a list of all paired devices; browser-to-desktop pairing was not found in this feature. Web Settings > Account > Linked devices (Unlink device) covers linked CLI, VS Code, Chrome and desktop devices, not phones.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and run Code: Remote Control. The panel titled Remote Control opens.
If a phone is paired, look for the line Connected to {phone} and the button Disconnect phone. If none is paired, you see Pair a phone and a QR code.
Click Disconnect phone. A dialog asks Disconnect {phone}? with the button Disconnect phone; confirm it.
Check that the panel no longer shows Connected to {phone} and returns to the pairing state, to compare with Expected.
S86.08.where: Command palette > Code: Remote Control (or type /remote-control in the chat box). The Remote Control panel shows Pair a phone, or Connected to {phone} with Disconnect phone.

labels.text: Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud

S86.09.note: Sign out runs at once with no confirmation dialog; if the AGI CLI on this machine stays signed in, a warning message appears.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the sidebar so the account row shows your account.
Click the More actions button in the sidebar header.
Click Sign out in the menu, below the account name.
Look at the menu again: the account name should read Not signed in and the item should now read Sign in, to compare with Expected.
S86.09.where: More actions (icon in the sidebar header) > Sign out, in the account row at the bottom of the menu. Also Command palette > Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud.

S86.23.needs: a saved approval (made by choosing Always allow on an approval prompt) and a signed-in CLI
S86.23.note: If the CLI offers permission rules, the picker title is Code, Permissions and shows a permissions view instead of Saved approvals, so the exact screen the tester sees may differ; the remove-confirmation wording was read from code only.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and run Code: Permissions, or type /permissions in the chat box.
Look for the picker titled Saved approvals with rows marked Always allowed or Always denied. If none are saved, the picker says No approvals are saved yet.
To have one to remove, first choose Always allow on an approval prompt in chat, then reopen Code: Permissions.
Click the remove action on a row and confirm Remove this saved approval?, then check the row is gone, to compare with Expected.
S86.23.where: Command palette > Code: Permissions (or type /permissions in the chat box). The picker opens with the title Saved approvals.

S86.24.needs: a workspace folder open and trusted; Bypass permissions needs the separate risk confirmation
S86.24.note: Expected says ask every time, auto-approve safe, autonomous; the code offers Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions, and no mode is labelled autonomous, so the mapping is unknown.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and run Code: Choose Agent Mode.
Pick Ask, then send a chat request that edits a file or runs a command.
Check the agent asks for approval before it acts.
Repeat with Auto (ordinary workspace edits run without prompting) and then Bypass permissions, which first asks for a risk confirmation; compare with Expected.
S86.24.where: Command palette > Code: Choose Agent Mode, or Code: Open Settings > Agent mode. Mode names are Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions.

S86.26.needs: a web account with at least two passkeys or security keys and access to the email on the account
S86.26.note: The VS Code app has no hardened-mode control; this is on the web account settings. The Settings > Security path comes from the support page apps/web/content/support/account-security.md, not from the navigation code, which was not verified.
steps: In the web app, sign in and open Settings, then the Security section.
Find the Advanced Account Security panel.
Click Turn on Advanced Account Security and follow its steps (passkeys or security keys, a code emailed to you, and recovery keys).
Once on, sign in again and check that a password or email code alone no longer gets you in, to compare with Expected.
S86.26.where: Web app (not inside VS Code): Settings > Security > Turn on Advanced Account Security (panel titled Advanced Account Security).
